dedupe_keys.name: on the effects of bat protection strategies on energy production and structural loads of wind farms

description: Pettas, Vasilis and colleagues describe this resource in the native deposit. The onshore-farm application compares static and dynamic bat-protection curtailment with an uncurtailed baseline. Long-term environmental and bat activity data drive wind-farm flow and mode-dependent aeroelastic fatigue surrogates. Energy losses and fatigue accumulation are aggregated across operating states and years. The source finds smaller energy losses under the evaluated dynamic strategies but channel-dependent fatigue effects. Transient-event assumptions and site climate constrain interpretation; the results do not establish universal ecological effectiveness. Zenodo provides the deposit with open access under cc-by-4.0. This record represents the documented application and its stated scope. Publication access does not imply that its underlying measurements or implementation are public. Coverage is limited to the stated experiment, model or application; transfer to other turbines, sites or operating regimes requires separate assessment. Publication date alone does not establish current maintenance. The application is based on the combination of environmental observations with fatigue-response surrogates.
